title: Knowledge check — 8 questions
note: Unlocks after the applied activity is submitted. Retakes are free and unlimited.

questions.prompt: Why are cycle time and closure rate described as blind to the product?
options: Because they are lagging indicators and report too late to act on
Because both score the same on the day of closure regardless of whether the finding will hold, so a matter closed fast on a record that collapses appears as a success for years
Because they are not comparable across organizations
Because they measure the investigator rather than the investigation
questions.explanation: Which is not an argument against speed: a matter left open is a harm continuing. It is an argument that the metrics you are measured on cannot see the thing you are for.

questions.prompt: Which of these appears on the module's list of what makes a finding hold?
options: A report under a defined page limit, so that decision-makers read it in full
A closure within the published timescale for the matter type
Every allegation has a resolution — including the ones that could not be resolved, recorded as unresolved, with why
Sign-off by a second investigator on every matter
questions.explanation: And note what the whole list omits: nothing about speed, volume, or tooling. A finding can hold in a matter that took four months and one that took eleven days.

questions.prompt: What does the module say about the 38% figure? `[V]`
options: 38% of ER teams have deployed AI for investigations

38% of organizations operate without a required investigation process — the least glamorous number in the study and the most consequential, because every capability in this track sits on top of a process
38% track substantiation by issue type
38% of matters are closed within the published timescale
questions.explanation: And the consequence is stated plainly: if you are in that 38%, the highest-value change available to you is not AI.

questions.prompt: Why is time-to-first-contact described as a different instrument from time-to-close?
options: Because it is easier to collect automatically
Because time-to-close measures how fast you finish, while time-to-first-contact measures how fast a person who raised something stops waiting in silence
Because it is the measure regulators ask for
Because it excludes matters that are withdrawn
questions.explanation: It correlates with trust in the process, willingness to report, and whether a matter escalates, and it is the one measure in the list you can start collecting this week.

questions.prompt: What is the caution about the published benchmark figures? `[V]`
options: They are unreliable because the study is vendor-sponsored
They describe organizations below 1,000 employees and so overstate small-employer maturity
They are aggregates about organizations, not targets — committing to reach a published rate commits you to a number rather than to accuracy
They should be treated as confidential to subscribers
questions.explanation: The study is vendor-sponsored *and* independently fielded with a disclosed sample, which is why it is usable; the real risk is turning a fact about the field into a goal, which is the failure Module 5 described.

questions.prompt: Why is AI in this function called a triage story rather than a productivity story?
options: Because triage is the highest-value application available

Because the expensive parts of the work — deciding which account to believe, whether precedent governs, what conduct amounted to — are the parts that may not be delegated, so what you get is recovered minutes rather than the same work faster
Because case volumes have doubled and triage is the only way to keep up
Because a model can route matters more consistently than a person
questions.explanation: And D is the specific thing Module 1 forbids, intake triage is a rung-five determination in rung-one clothing.

questions.prompt: Where does the track argue the recovered minutes should go, and why?
options: Into closing more matters, since backlog is the most visible harm
Into better-written reports, since the report is the record
Into rung two, corroboration — least visible, first cut under pressure, where cases are won and lost, and the rung where AI is genuinely permitted at scale
Into training, since capability gaps cause most record defects
questions.explanation: A and B are two of the three places the minutes go on their own. The third is the queue, where they are absorbed invisibly and you cannot say what the deployment bought.

questions.prompt: What is the second half of the bet's fourth term?
options: Who signs off on the change
What you would turn off — including, honestly, anything your team is already using on case content without sanction
What you would do if the measure improved faster than expected
How the change would be communicated to employees
questions.explanation: For some readers the strongest bet available is not a deployment at all: a sanctioned tool replacing an unsanctioned one, and a conversation that surfaces what is already happening. A bet that ignores what your team is already doing is a bet on a fiction.
